newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Alston says Telstra job cuts not due to sale.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Alston says Telstra job cuts not due to sale.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston said on Friday that job losses at state-owned telecommunications giant Telstra Corp Ltd were not related to its planned partial sale.
"What is happening now is not privatisation-related," Alston told reporters.
Earlier, Telstra said it planned further staff cuts of 13,000 in 1996/97 on top of a previously announced 9,000.
Alston said the job losses were a necessary part of improving Telstra's competitiveness in the lead-up to deregulation of the telecommunications industry in July 1997.

Alston quoted Telstra chief executive Frank Blount as saying that job cuts at Telstra "were not motivated by the impending privatisation, but in anticipation of aggressive competition when the market was fully deregulated next July".
The government plans to raise A$8.0 billion through the sale of one-third of Telstra.
A Senate Committee report recommended against the sale earlier this week, saying there was no evidence to support the government's claim that the economy and consumers would benefit.
However, the committee was dominated by the Opposition Labor Party and the left-leaning Australian Democrats, both of which oppose the partial privatisation.
Telstra earlier reported a 35 percent rise in annual net profit to A$2.3 billion.
